subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:23:00 -0400
Subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up (Acme Health)

Hi Sam / Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciated the chance to dig into Acme Health's security and privacy constraints. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard from you:
- PII ingestion will include patient names, limited PHI in free-text fields, and identifiers (no SSNs).
- You require data residency in the US for production workloads.
- Encryption at-rest with customer-managed keys (BYOK) is a requirement for the primary dataset.
- Audit logging for inference requests (request IDs, timestamps, model variant) is needed for investigations, with a 1-year retention window.

2) Redwood capabilities (short):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced for all endpoints.
- At-rest: default AES-256 encryption; we support KMS integrations for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS).
- HSM/BYOK: We support encrypted key wrapping and can integrate with Cloud KMS for BYOK. Dedicated/private deployments support HSM-backed key stores on request.
- Logging: Request/response metadata can be retained in audit logs; payload logging is configurable and can be disabled/hashed for PII-sensitive flows.

3) Questions we promised to confirm:
- Can you confirm whether Acme will require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2) or encrypted KMS BYOK is sufficient?
- Is the 1-year retention requirement for logs inclusive of request metadata only, or does it include any cached prefixes/KV entries we might store for performance?

Next steps:
- Dylan (cc'd) will follow up tomorrow with a short technical note that outlines our KMS integration options and where HSM-backed key stores would fit into a Dedicated/Private deployment.
- I'll send the SOC2 summary + KMS integration diagram for your security team.
- If helpful, propose a 30-minute follow-up with your security architect next week to lock down the exact artchitecture and timeline.

Deliverables: SOC2-Summary.pdf (attached), kms-integration-diagram.png (attached).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up (Acme Health)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our notes. A couple clarifications from our security team: 

- We prefer HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 2 or higher) for production-level PHI workflows. If HSM is not possible, we need documented compensating controls.
- The 1-year retention applies to request metadata only; we cannot retain request payloads containing PII. Any caching of KV/prefixes that would persist PII is not acceptable. We could accept hashed prefixes with a documented hashing scheme.
- For audit purposes, we need exportable logs (s3 or secure transfer) with integrity checks.

Can Dylan include an entry on whether your Dedicated or Private deployment supports an HSM-backed KMS and the effort to set up a BYOK flow (key creation/rotation/zeroization)? Also please include any limitations around caching and whether those can be disabled per-customer.

Best,
Sam
Sam Patel
Security Architect | Acme Health
sam.patel@acmehealth.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS follow-up (Acme Health)

Hi Sam — thanks for the clarifications. Quick technical responses (high level):

HSM / BYOK:
- Dedicated & Private deployments: We can integrate with customer HSMs (via Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM appliances) and support FIPS 140-2 validated modules. For cloud-managed HSM (e.g., AWS CloudHSM), Redwood can be configured to use keys that never leave the HSM.
- Hosted (multi-tenant) mode: We support BYOK via cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) with key policies that restrict access; however, hosted mode does not currently support direct customer HSM attachments (we can discuss an enterprise exception with Dedicated capacity).
- Key rotation/zeroization: Rotation can be automated; zeroization procedures exist for Private deployments where customer keys are destroyed by policy. We'll document timelines and automation steps in the follow-up doc.

Caching & KV:
- KV/prefix caching is controllable per-route. For PII-sensitive routes we can disable caching entirely or enable hashing of prefixes with customer-provided salt. When caching is disabled there is a throughput impact; we'll quantify this for your typical qps in a separate note.

Logging & Exports:
- Audit logs (request id, timestamp, model, route, response status) can be exported to your S3 bucket via secure transfer. Logs can be delivered daily and signed (SHA256) to support integrity checks. Payloads (full request or response) will not be logged unless explicitly enabled by you.

Attachments: attaching an "encryption-config-options.docx" that outlines options (Hosted BYOK, Dedicated w/CloudHSM, Private w/on-prem HSM) and estimated timelines/effort. Also attached a diagram showing where KMS/HSM fits into Dedicated and Private deployments.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical deep dive with our infra team and your security engineers next Thursday (10/21) or Friday (10/22).

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
